We are happy to announce Quantum Computing Hackathon in association with IBM Quantum under the "Qiskit Fall Fest 2021" which is taking place at many universities across the world including Ahmedabad University. Check out more about Qiskit Fall Fest here.( https://qiskitfallfest.hypeinnovation.com/) Quantum Computing utilizes quantum phenomena like superposition, entanglement, and interference to solve problems and performs calculations that classical computers could take billions of years to do.   If you are interested in learning more about quantum computing or just curious about this upcoming technology we encourage you to join us. You don't need to know anything about quantum computing to join this event. We will have lectures and workshops to equip you with all the information you need to start building your quantum project.  You can form a team of a maximum of 5 people and work on building a quantum project. If you do not have a team, you'll get the opportunity to network with your fellow participants and form the team during the event.  The event is going to take place in a hybrid mode on 16th and 17th October 2021 at Ahmedabad University. The event will start from 9 AM onwards. If you wish to attend the event offline you must have taken the second dose of the Covid vaccine. Students must bring their own laptops. The seats to attend offline are limited so please register soon! INAUGURATION OF PAKISTAN’S FIRST NATIONAL CYBER SECURITY ACADEMY  23 November, 2021: Dr Arif Alvi, President Islamic Republic of Pakistan, inaugurated country's first ever National Cyber Security Academy at the opening ceremony of International Conference on Cyber Warfare & Security 2021 (ICCWS 2021) at PAF Complex, Isamabad. Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, Chief of the Air Staff, Pakistan Air Force received President Alvi at the conference venue. The event was also attended by Air Marshal (Retd) Javaid Ahmed, Vice Chancellor Air University and Air Vice Marshal Abbas Ghumman, Director General C4I PAF along with civil-military and foreign dignitaries.  While addressing the ceremony, President Dr Arif Alvi declared Cyber Security as a global threat having implications on National Security of the country. The President appreciated industry-academia collaboration, where PAF worked closely with the Air University and HEC in establishing country’s first ever Cyber Security Academy. Terming it as a historic occasion, the President called for pursuit of excellence in Cyber domain.  Chief of the Air Staff’s vision on evolving Cyber domain has defined PAF’s role in contributing to Cyber Security objectives under National Cyber Security Policy 2021. PAF has worked closely with academia to strengthen HR talent and R&D efforts in the Cyber domain. Through effective industry-academia linkages supported by comprehensive R&D setups, PAF would transform into an effective, ubiquitous and highly responsive Cyber Force.  Speaking at the occasion, Air Vice Marshal Abbas Ghumman, Director General C4I PAF, highlighted PAF’s contributions in establishment of Cyber Security Academy and successful conduct of the ICCWS along with Cyber Security Industry Exhibition. Air Vice Marshal Abbas also highlighted PAF’s plan to establish its own Cyber Command supported by a Cyber Technology Park and Cyber Center of Excellence under National Aerospace Science and Technology Park (NASTP).  Air Marshal (Retd) Javaid Ahmed, Vice Chancellor Air University on the occasion expressed that overall objective of the Cyber Security Academy was to produce trained Cyber experts for government, industry, public and private sector organizations to address emerging Cyber Security threats.  After inauguration of Cyber Academy, President Arif Alvi along with Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, Chief of the Air Staff, Pakistan Air Force visited Cyber Security Industry Exhibition at conference’s venue. Chief of the Air Staff briefed the President regarding various initiatives being pursued by PAF in collaboration with local and foreign technology experts.  *PAF SPOKESPERSON*

*Output 15* of Terminal 2020 an explanation: For the Out 15 the answer is actually 3 but its actually tricky for most the actual solution is quite different from the expected solution let's pass an address *1000* to the function and move to the line **p2 = *p1 / *p2;* -> the expected output we get is 60/20 = 3; after which we move to the next line **p2++; * -> most people will assume that we are incrementing 3 by 1 making it 4 but what really happens is that we increment the address making it *1004* and we don't increment the value of p2 so now whatever value is assigned it's actually assigned to a completely new address so no matter how many times we run the loop the value of the original p2 address will remain 3 and as we actually passed the address *1000* it has been assigned a value of 3 so when we actually print the value of p2 we actually are printing the original address of *1000* the point to remember here is to actually treat it as an address instead of value. Covering remaining concepts like friend functions,member wise assignments and composition.

1. When an object of class is created, constructor is called, either parameterised or non-parameterised.  2. When object is created in main function, destructor of that object is called right before the termination of program or the end of main program.  3. When an object is created in a non-main function, constructor is called when the object is created. Destructor of that object is called when the *scope of that non-main function ends* Scope of non-main function is the end of function body(curly ending brace)
Deconstructors do not work when the program ends abnormally what that means is when we use a function like exit(): deconstructor wont be called

Only for automatic local objects destructor is not called with exit(), otherwise destructor is called when we use exit() with global objects or static local objects.  Moreover destructor is never called when abort() is used regardless of the scope of object.

Then it will prepare a report and it will dispatch the item after checking the availability and then receive the product and then give it to the user.Design the application for the above problem description.    5. ONLINE COURSE RESERVATION:  Create a link between a student and administrator in which student select the college thenviewing the college details and check whether the seats are filled in that college. Design the application for the above problem description.    7. *Where have you seen Data structures in real-time applications?*  𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐜𝐤: 1) UNDO option 2) Text editor: you push letter by letter to the stack so you erase back. 3) Recursion(inbuilt stack)  𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐮𝐞: 1) Your browser deletes the history past one month. 2) If you delete a picture on your phone, it will be the "recently delete" folder which says "the images will be deleted permanently after one week". Here all the images are stored in the queue so it's easier to pop from the rear based on the image deletion date. 3) Waiting list: during online registrations, sometimes you'll be put on the waiting list. basically, all the requests will be stored in the queue.  𝐋𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐞𝐝 𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐭: 1) Browser's Next and Previous Button: a linked list of URLs 2) music player where you can play the next or previous song. (Doubly linked list). 3) In the ludo game, It has to pass the chance to each player in a circular fashion (circular linked list).  𝐓𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐬: 1) File system: Folders and subfolders (N-ary tree). 2) e-commerce websites : category -> subcategories -> products 3) Auto-suggestion when you google (Trie)  𝐆𝐫𝐚𝐩𝐡𝐬: 1) Uber, Ola cab booking: show nearest available cars (BFS) 2) Maven dependencies build order ( Topological sorting (DFS)) 3) While booking bus/flights, you get a list of available routes. 4) In Facebook, users are considered to be the vertices and if they are friends then there is an edge running between them. *Things To Do For Trip* 1-Bring some basic medicines for nausea and pain killers etc. 2-Bring Water bottles and some Candies, chocolates etc cuz sugar level drops in hikes. 3- Fully charge your mobile phones and bring power banks. 4- Should have at least Rs.1500 for breakfast, lunch and also keep some extra *cash* with yourself. 5- University card and CNIC is must. 6- Share your WhatsApp live location for at least 8 hours with me and some family member. 7- Remain in groups of 4,5 or more. 8- Don't wear sandals, sneakers or pumps etc instead wear some durable joggers. 9- Bring an extra pair of socks cuz shoes easily slip on snow so you'll have to wear it on shoes. 10- Don't rush for the hike, maintain your normal pace. 11- Bring a small bag pack but remember to keep it lighter otherwise it won't let you enjoy yourself. 12- Get sufficient sleep otherwise you'll be tired soon.

پیارے رضاکاروں،  میں معاون مشن کے لیے آپ کی ناقابل یقین لگن اور سخت محنت کے لیے آپ کا شکریہ ادا کرنے کے لیے ایک لمحہ نکالنا چاہتا ہوں۔ آپ کی انتھک کوششوں نے پہلے ہی بہت بڑا اثر ڈالا ہے، لیکن ہمیں اپنے مقصد کے قریب پہنچنے کے لیے اب پہلے سے زیادہ آپ کی مدد کی ضرورت ہے۔  جیسا کہ آپ جانتے ہیں، ہم فی الحال پراجیکٹ کے عطیہ کیس کو بند کرنے کے لیے چندہ اکٹھا کرنے کی سمت کام کر رہے ہیں۔ جب کہ ہم نے ترقی کی ہے، ہمارے پاس اپنے ہدف تک پہنچنے کے لیے ابھی بھی راستے باقی ہیں۔ لیکن مجھے اس میں کوئی شک نہیں کہ آپ کے جذبے اور جوش و جذبے سے ہم مل کر اسے حاصل کر سکتے ہیں۔  میں جانتا ہوں کہ جب ہمیں رکاوٹوں اور ناکامیوں کا سامنا کرنا پڑتا ہے تو یہ حوصلہ شکنی ہو سکتا ہے، لیکن میں آپ سے گزارش کرتا ہوں کہ اپنے مقصد پر توجہ مرکوز رکھیں اور آگے بڑھتے رہیں۔ ہر عطیہ شمار ہوتا ہے، اور آپ کی ہر کوشش ہمیں اپنے ہدف تک پہنچنے کے ایک قدم کے قریب لاتی ہے۔  لہذا میں آپ سے کہتا ہوں کہ اس بات کو پھیلاتے رہیں، اپنے نیٹ ورکس تک پہنچیں، اور اپنی تخلیقی صلاحیتوں اور وسائل کو دوسروں کو عطیہ کرنے کی ترغیب دینے کے لیے استعمال کریں۔ آئیے ایک حقیقی فرق کرنے اور حقیقی معنوں میں کچھ حاصل کرنے کے لیے مل کر کام کریں۔  ہمارے مشن کے لیے آپ کی غیر متزلزل وابستگی کا شکریہ۔ آپ کی لگن اور محنت واقعی قابل تعریف ہے، اور مجھے کوئی شک نہیں کہ آپ کی مسلسل کوششوں سے ہم کامیاب ہوں گے۔  Regards, Director, Muaawin PIEAS chapter

https://aibusiness.com/nlp/to-make-ai-perform-better-researchers-turn-to-human-style-prompts  Phrasing can influence AI output The DeepMind study also found that certain phrases influenced the AI's output. Prompts like "let's think step by step" led the AI models to yield more accurate results when evaluated against math problem datasets.  The researchers discovered that the prompt *"Take a deep breath and work on this problem step by step" was most effective with Google's PaLM 2 language model. This phrase reached the highest accuracy score of 80.2% when tested against GSM8K, a dataset of grade-school math word problems. In comparison, PaLM 2, without any special prompting, achieved only a 34% accuracy on GSM8K, while the classic prompt "Let’s think step by step" reached a 71.8% accuracy score.*  LLMs respond well to human-like prompts because they are trained on human language conversational data such as Reddit threads and movie scripts, said Michael Kearns, a professor of Computer and Information Science at the University of Pennsylvania, who was not part of the DeepMind team, in an interview.
